title: Four Checks Before You Launch
topic: Security checklist for AI-built (vibe-coded) apps, after the Lovable flaw and the RedAccess scan
notes: Content from Shazim's brief; sources in research.md. Check 2 nuance added (publishable keys are fine, secret/service-role keys never) — accuracy fix. CTA is a DM, no keyword guide.

cover.title: AI-built apps were found leaking data
cover.sub: Four checks to run on yours first.

slides.title: One scan. 5,000 leaks.
slides.body: A May scan of apps built on AI app builders found thousands exposing sensitive data.

slides.title: Change the ID in the address bar
slides.body: Log in as one user, then swap the ID for another user's.

mock.title: logged in as alex
mock.who: you, as alex, change one number:

outcomes.t: Sam's invoice loads — stop and fix it

slides.note: This was the flaw that hit Lovable in April.

slides.title: No secrets in the browser
slides.body: Search the code that runs in the browser for API keys and secrets. There should be none.

mock.title: terminal
lines: # searching the built browser bundle…

slides.note: Publishable keys (like Supabase's anon key) are fine. Secret and service-role keys, never.

slides.title: Lock every table
slides.body: On Supabase, turn on row level security for every table — then test it with a second account.

slides.title: Break the payment on purpose
slides.body: In test mode, double-click pay and drop your connection mid-payment.
slides.note: One charge, every time. Anything else is a refund waiting to happen.

slides.title: Restore a backup — once
slides.body: Before you ever need it. A backup you've never restored is a hope, not a backup.

slides.title: $5K build vs $15K build
slides.body: These checks are most of what the extra money buys.
